claims.text: A multi-scale ML workflow using grain size, phase fraction, short-range order, and mechanical-test data can reliably predict thermomechanical processing routes for HEAs.
The predicted processing routes can simultaneously enhance strength, ductility, Young's modulus, and fracture resistance.
A typical starting multi-principal-element alloy contains at least five elements in near-equiatomic proportions.
Atom-probe tomography can provide species-specific short-range-order maps for use as microstructural descriptors.
Integrating characterization and mechanical data can identify targeted rolling, forging, and annealing modifications that improve mechanical performance.
HEA phase formation can be predicted with data-driven features derived from DFT-calculated pairwise elemental interactions.
The phases and number of phases present strongly affect HEA strength, ductility, and fracture resistance.
Heat treatment can alter short-range order in medium- or high-entropy alloys.
Refining and controlling grain size, short-range-ordered regions, and secondary-phase dispersion mitigates brittle-phase formation.
The proposed controlled microstructure fosters dislocation multiplication, twinning, and other ductile deformation pathways.
A soft BCC matrix combined with shear-resistant secondary precipitates can provide concurrent ductility and strengthening.
ML-guided processing can optimize solution and precipitation strengthening concurrently with twinning and dislocation cross-slip.
Conventional multi-principal-element alloys typically have yield strengths of approximately 1–1.2 GPa.
The ML-guided approach will increase strength by 15–20% relative to conventional multi-principal-element alloys.
The strength increase will occur while ductility and fracture toughness are maintained or improved.
Current HEA design relies heavily on trial-and-error or partial optimization and often trades ductility against strength.
Model effectiveness will diminish for compositions or processing conditions outside the training domain.
Extremely high temperatures or strain rates may activate deformation mechanisms absent from the model and invalidate its predictions.
Insufficient compositional coverage or incomplete microstructural descriptors may cause overfitting and poor generalization.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says the workflow can reliably predict successful routes, while the uncertainty field says model reliability across alloy families remains unconfirmed and may be limited by overfitting.

The hypothesis promises simultaneous enhancements in all four properties, but the predicted outcome quantifies only strength, allows ductility and toughness merely to be maintained, and gives no expected improvement in Young's modulus.
